newsitem.title: GERMANY: German stocks advance, dismiss slight dollar slip.
newsitem.headline: German stocks advance, dismiss slight dollar slip.

text.p: German shares got the week off to a strong start on Monday, with prices approaching record high levels as the market shrugged off comments from G7 leaders this weekend which seemed designed to cap the dollar's gains.

The 30-share blue chip DAX index ended bourse trade on Monday up nearly 1.5 percent at 3,184.36 points, and prices held steady in afternoon screen-based dealings, which the IBIS DAX closed at 3,185.72.
"No-one seems to be worried about the G7 comments and stocks influenced by the dollar, such as the big exporters, are still in favour," said one trader.

"While the momentum is there, let the cash roll in. We're looking for arguments to target new highs. This has been a fantastic year so far and people are wary of changing the scenario," another Frankfurt trader said.
However a factor weighing on volumes in floor trade was the Fasching pre-Lenten carnival, which runs until Wednesday and is expected to keep activity limited, especially in Frankfurt and Duesseldorf.
Tuesday afternoon is a half-day public holiday in many parts of southern and central Germany to celebrate Fasching, but both IBIS DAX trade and bourse will take place as normal.

Siemens AG was one of the big gainers, boosted by a series of positive analysts reports last week. The electronics giant ended bourse trade up 1.22 marks at 87.02 marks, before paring those gains to end IBIS at 86.97 marks.

Building company Hochtief AG also ended higher after the magazine Focus quoted its management board chairman Hans-Peter Keitel saying he saw a future shift away from construction to more complex civil engineering projects.
The company ended bourse trade up 1.90 marks at 70.80 marks and rose to 71.50 marks in later trade.
Software company SAP AG ended floor trade up 2.80 marks at 256 marks and later rose to 256.50 marks, after it said it was in a consulting venture with Software AG.
